cards.text: Moses, Israel's leader, is talking to the people, walking them back through their own story. They marched up to fight without the LORD and got chased off by the Amorites like a swarm of bees (Deuteronomy 1:42-44). Now they turn back toward the wilderness by way of the Red Sea, just as the LORD told Moses.

cards.question: For many days after turning back, where does Israel wander?

cards.text: Then the LORD speaks to Moses: "You have been wandering around this hill country long enough; turn to the north…" Friend, I spent YEARS in the back of a junk drawer, and I would have paid good money to hear those words!

Next, Israel will pass through Seir, home of the descendants of Esau, Jacob's twin brother (Genesis 25:24-26). The LORD calls them Israel's brothers, so friend, this isn't a border crossing, it's a family reunion.

cards.question: The LORD tells Israel to treat Esau's descendants in Seir as enemies.
Esau's people will be afraid of Israel, so the LORD tells Israel to be very ___.

cards.text: And the LORD is clear: don't provoke them, and Israel gets none of their land, not even a footprint. That's not "keep off the grass," friend, that's "don't even TOUCH the welcome mat!"

cards.question: Why won't Israel get any of Esau's land?

answers.text: God gave Mount Seir to Esau

cards.question: Israel will need food and water while passing through Seir. How does the LORD say they get it?

answers.text: They pay for it in silver

cards.text: Then Moses stops to remind them. The LORD has blessed all the work of their hands and watched over their journey through this vast wilderness.

cards.question: Moses says the LORD has been with Israel these forty years, and they have lacked ___.
Israel passes by its brothers, the descendants of Esau in Seir, and keeps going.

cards.text: They turn away from the Arabah road, which comes up from Elath and Ezion-geber, and take the road of the Wilderness of Moab.
Moab is up ahead. The Moabites are descendants of Lot, Abraham's nephew (Genesis 12:5; 19:36-37), and the LORD has a word for Moses about them.

cards.question: The LORD tells Moses that Israel should drive the Moabites out of their land.
Why won't Israel get any of Moab's land?

answers.text: God gave Ar to Lot's descendants
Moab's cities are too far away
Moses made a deal with Moab

cards.text: Then the passage drops in a note: the Emites used to live there, a people great and many, as tall as the Anakites. The Moabites called them Emites, but like the Anakites, they were regarded as Rephaim.
Same kind of history in Seir. The Horites used to live there, but Esau's descendants drove them out and settled in their place.

cards.question: The note compares Esau's people settling in Seir to something else. What is it?

answers.text: What Israel did in its own land
What Moab did to the Ammonites

cards.text: Back to the LORD's words to Moses: "Now arise and cross over the Brook of Zered." Back at Kadesh, the LORD's command was go up, and Israel dug in their heels (Deuteronomy 1:21, 26).

cards.question: This time, Israel obeys and crosses the Brook of Zered.

cards.text: Then Moses tallies up the trip from Kadesh-barnea to the Brook of Zered. Back at Kadesh, the LORD swore that not one man of that evil generation would see the good land (Deuteronomy 1:35).

cards.question: The trip from Kadesh-barnea to the Brook of Zered took ___ years.
The trip from Kadesh-barnea to the Brook of Zered lasted until what happened?

answers.text: That generation of fighting men had all died

cards.text: Moses doesn't soften it. The LORD's hand was against them until every one of those fighting men had perished from the camp.

When all those fighting men have died, the LORD tells Moses, "Today you are going to cross the border of Moab at Ar." Thirty-eight years of traveling and now it's TODAY, friend, and I would have had my apron on before He finished the sentence!
The LORD has more: soon Israel will get close to the Ammonites. They're descendants of Lot too (Genesis 19:38), and the LORD has a word about them.

cards.question: The LORD tells Israel to harass and provoke the Ammonites.
The LORD says Israel will get ___ of the land of the Ammonites.

cards.text: Then another note: Ammon's land was regarded as land of the Rephaim too, who used to live there. The Ammonites called them Zamzummites, a people great and many, as tall as the Anakites.

cards.question: The Zamzummites were great and many. Who destroyed them from before the Ammonites?
The note adds that the LORD had done the same for Esau's descendants in Seir, destroying the Horites from before them.

cards.text: And one last note: the Avvim, who lived in villages as far as Gaza, were destroyed by the Caphtorites, who came out of Caphtor and settled in their place. That's where we'll pause, friend, because Moses is nowhere near done telling this journey.
